'''Herman Brenner White''' (born 28 September 1948) is an American physicist who works at [[Fermilab]]. He won the 2010 [[American Physical Society]] Edward A Bouchet Award and became a fellow of the American Physical Society in 2025.

== Early life and education ==
White was born in [[Tuskegee, Alabama]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.idvl.org/sciencemakers/Bio12.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160416055519/http://www.idvl.org/sciencemakers/Bio12.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=April 16, 2016|title=Biography Page for Herman White|website=www.idvl.org|date=September 2015 |access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> His mother, Susie Mae Fort White, worked at John Andrew Hospital and his father, Herman Brenner White Senior, served in the military.<ref name=":0" /> He studied at the [[Tuskegee, Alabama|Tuskegee]] Institute High School, where he became interested in nuclear engineering.<ref name=":0" /> He was raised in a segregated community.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsbp.org/nsbp-news/bhm-physics-profiles/2017-honorees/17-herman-white-jr|title=Herman White, Jr.|last=Roberson|first=Stephen|website=www.nsbp.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> He saw his role in the civil rights movement as being an exceptional student who could prove that black people deserved equal access to education.<ref name=":0" /> He studied nuclear physics at [[Earlham College]], before joining [[Michigan State University]], earning a bachelor's degree in physics in 1970.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/herman-brenner-white-jr|title=Herman Brenner White, Jr. {{!}} The HistoryMakers|website=www.thehistorymakers.org|language=en|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> White was awarded an [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] Fellowship to study at [[CERN]], and also worked as a research associate at [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> He completed his master's degree in 1974.<ref name=":0" /> He joined [[Fermilab]] in 1974, where he was the first African-American physicist to be appointed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.c2st.org/fermilabs-first-black-particle-physicist-dr-herman-b-white/|title=Fermilab's First Black Particle Physicist - Dr. Herman B. White {{!}} The Chicago Council on Science and Technology|website=www.c2st.org|date=3 February 2017 |language=en-US|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
White held various roles at [[Fermilab]] since joining in 1974.<ref name=":2" /> Working with his supervisor, Ray Stefanski, he developed a simple formula to calculate neutrino flux.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.fnal.gov/2011/01/ray-stefanski-retires-after-41-years/|title=Ray Stefanski retires after 41 years {{!}} News|website=news.fnal.gov|date=5 January 2011|language=en-US|access-date=2018-09-30|archive-date=2018-09-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930231647/http://news.fnal.gov/2011/01/ray-stefanski-retires-after-41-years/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1976 he joined [[Yale University]] as a research fellow. He joined [[Florida State University]] for his doctoral studies, earning a PhD in 1991.<ref name=":2" /> He joined the [[Universidad Autónoma de San Luis Potosí]] to work on [[kaon]]s. In 1994, White was appointed the Illinois Research Corridor Fellow and adjunct professor at [[North Central College]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://ed.fnal.gov/symposium/speakers/2007white.html|title=Fermilab's 2007 Nature of Science Symposium|website=ed.fnal.gov|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> He also worked on the [[neutrino oscillation]] experiment (E701) and [[SciBooNE]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fnal.gov/pub/today/HermanWhiteAward_Oct142009.html|title=Fermilab Today|website=www.fnal.gov|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> He studies neutrino cross-sections and muon conversion.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/the-100-muon-detector|title=The $100 muon detector|work=symmetry magazine|access-date=2018-09-30|language=en}}</ref> In 2006 his life story was recorded by the [[HistoryMakers]] of Chicago as part of the oral history archives.<ref name=":2" />

White supports students from diverse backgrounds in their careers in physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://uswip.org/Delegation.html#White|title=6th International Conference on Women in Physics: U.S. Delegation|website=uswip.org|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> In 2010 White was awarded the [[American Physical Society]] [[Edward A. Bouchet]] Award for his work on the [[Tevatron|Tevatron experiment]] and outstanding public service.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Herman&last_nm=White&year=2010|title=2018 Norman F. Ramsey Prize in Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, and in Precision Tests of Fundamental Laws and Symmetries Recipient|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> He serves on the advisory board for [[QuarkNet]], [[National Society of Black Physicists]] and the [[Illinois Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":1" /> He is a member of the Teachers Academy for Mathematics and Science in Chicago.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fermilabcommunity.org/members/herman-white/|title=Herman White {{!}} Fermilab Community Advisory Board|website=www.fermilabcommunity.org|language=en-US|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> He served on the advisory panel for the [[United States Department of Energy]] and [[National Science Foundation]].<ref name=":4" /> He ran for congress in the 11th congressional district of [[Illinois]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hermanwhiteforcongress.com/|title=Herman White for Congress {{!}} 11th Congressional District|website=www.hermanwhiteforcongress.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-09-30|archive-date=2018-09-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930231431/http://www.hermanwhiteforcongress.com/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2017 he appeared in a series of online videos for ''Science the Day!''.<ref>{{Citation|last=Science The Day!|title=Fermilab's First Black Particle Physicist - Dr. Herman B. White|date=2017-02-03|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RsVcyweTfKM|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Science The Day!|title=Dr. Herman B. White: Particle Physics & Romantic Love|date=2017-02-09|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FtSTqqKtduE|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> He took part in [[The Story Collider]] in [[Batavia, Illinois]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.storycollider.org/shows/2018/5/12/batavia-il-fermilab|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180721110003/https://www.storycollider.org/shows/2018/5/12/batavia-il-fermilab|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 21, 2018|title=Batavia, IL - Physics|website=The Story Collider|language=en-US|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://radiopublic.com/the-story-collider-o6NYDW/ep/s1!7f989|title=The Story Collider – Leaving Home: Stories about the places we're from – 33:08|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> In 2025, he became a fellow of the American Physical Society "For inspiring leadership and advocacy for physics, science education, and communication with policy makers, governments and the public, and for outstanding contributions to several areas of high energy physics."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Forum on Physics and Society Fellowship |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship/fps-fellowship |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
